Gen.1.sp: The narrator; God speaks in v.3
wr: Not named in Genesis. Jesus speaks of Moses as one who wrote of him.
gr: The opening of the record: before the heavens and the earth existed.

wr: This psalm has no title; no writer is named.
au: Not stated; a poem about anyone who walks in either way.
gr: Sets the one who delights in the law of the LORD against the ungodly.

wr: David, according to the psalm's title.
au: Addressed to God; given to the chief Musician.
gr: Written after the prophet Nathan came to David over Bathsheba.

Isa.11.sp: The prophet, speaking of one to come
gr: Prophesied in the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

Isa.53.sp: The prophet, speaking of the servant
gr: Prophesied in the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah.

wr: Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, of the priests in Anathoth.
au: The house of Israel and the house of Judah.
gr: Jeremiah's ministry ran to the carrying away of Jerusalem captive.
Here God promises a new covenant.

wr: Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi.
au: The captives, the people of Israel in exile.
gr: Written among the captives by the river Chebar, in the land of the Chaldeans.
The land had been stripped by successive swarms of locusts.

wr: The Gospel does not name its writer within the text.
au: His disciples, with the multitudes nearby.
gr: John the Baptist had just been imprisoned; Jesus had begun preaching that the kingdom of heaven was at hand.
Crowds had come from Galilee, Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judaea and beyond Jordan.

wr: The Gospel does not name its writer within the text.
au: The same mountain audience: disciples and multitudes.
gr: Spoken as a warning about false prophets.
The crowd noticed he taught with authority, not as the scribes.

John.1.sp: The writer, a disciple of Jesus
wr: The disciple whom Jesus loved says he wrote these things.
au: Not named; written so that readers might believe.
gr: The prologue introduces the Word before John the Baptist enters as a witness.

au: His disciples, on the night Judas went out.
gr: Judas had gone out into the night; Jesus had said, Arise, let us go hence.
Jesus was preparing them for his going away.

Acts.2.sp: Peter, an apostle, quoting God through Joel
wr: Not named; the writer addresses Theophilus as in a former treatise.
au: The men of Judaea and all who dwelt at Jerusalem.
gr: The day of Pentecost; they were filled with the Holy Ghost and spoke with other tongues.
Some in the crowd mocked them as drunk, and Peter answered.

wr: Paul, an apostle sent not of men but by Jesus Christ.
au: The churches of Galatia, where Paul first preached in weakness.
gr: Some were troubling them and perverting the gospel.
They were being pressed to be circumcised.
